distanceRationale: Tau Ceti already has abelian varieties over a field (dimension, base change, tangent space), abstract divisor-class Pic⁰ with degree splitting and a divisor-level Abel–Jacobi class, function-field genus and Riemann–Roch spaces, and basic cohomology of sheaves of modules on schemes. distanceRationale: The library has scheme morphism properties, locally constant flat rank, relative normalization and the Hopf-algebra/affine-group-scheme correspondence (Mathlib). Nothing yet exists on elliptic curves as group schemes over an arbitrary base: no projective Weierstrass scheme model, relative Picard/Poincaré duality, scheme-theoretic Weil pairing, Drinfeld level structures, Katz–Mazur moduli formalism, fppf quotients, deformation theory, p-divisible groups, Serre–Tate theory, regularity theorems or coarse moduli. distanceRationale: Mathlib has ProfiniteGrp with limits and completions, finite Sylow theory and Frattini subgroups. Tau Ceti has built most of Layers 0–3: supernatural order and index with Lagrange, profinite Sylow existence, containment and conjugacy, the maximal pro-p quotient with its universal property, the pro-p Frattini subgroup with Burnside, topological finite generation and the Hopfian property. Still missing are free profinite and free pro-p groups with their universal properties, presentations with extensions, embedding problems and the H¹/H² rank interpretations, Golod–Shafarevich, cohomological dimension of pro-p groups including Serre's freeness theorem, Demushkin groups with duality and orientation, the central-tower comparison method, and Labute's classification. These form several layers of advanced graduate-to-research theory that also depend on unfinished continuous-cohomology infrastructure.

distanceRationale: Mathlib supplies quadratic forms, diagonalization, quaternion algebras and the Brauer group carrier. Tau Ceti has built Layers 0–1 and part of 2–3: the RegularFormClass carrier with discriminants, chain equivalence of diagonal forms, Witt decomposition, cancellation and extension, hyperbolic planes, Cartan–Dieudonné, the quaternion norm form with split and Steinberg relations, and a nontrivial quaternion Brauer class. Missing are the Witt ring with its fundamental ideal and Pfister forms, the four-fold splitting criterion, the Hasse and Clifford invariants, the quadratic defect and local Hilbert symbol, the local classification by (dim, d, s), the crossed-product comparison Br(K)[2] ≅ H²(G_K, μ₂) with the cup–norm theorem, Stiefel–Whitney classes, and the Scharlau transfer with Kahn's relative formula. These layers sit on the unfinished local-field, continuous-cohomology and class-field-theory suppliers, and Kahn's formula is research-level.

distanceRationale: Mathlib supplies Hopf algebras, group objects, abstract root data and Coxeter groups. Tau Ceti has built most of Layers 0–6 over a field: the Hopf/affine-group-scheme dictionary and functor of points, comodules with Tannakian reconstruction, Hopf ideals, fppf quotients and components, tangent spaces, Jordan decomposition, multiplicative-type groups and tori, unipotent and solvable radicals with Lie–Kolchin, and the reductive and semisimple predicates. It also has pieces of Layer 7: existence of geometric Borel subgroups, dynamic parabolics and Levi decompositions, GLₙ root data, torus-level special isogenies. Still missing are conjugacy of Borel subgroups and maximal tori, the root datum and Bruhat decomposition of a general reductive group, the isomorphism and existence (classification) theorems, and the explicitly constructed pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes over ℤ with root subgroups and the G₂/F₄ special isogenies. These are several deep layers of SGA 3–level theory.

distanceRationale: Layers 0–5 are essentially in Tau Ceti on top of Mathlib's Gaussian, Gamma, Beta and Poisson measures: the uniform measure, the new scalar families from Laplace to hypergeometric, pgfs, the incomplete gamma and beta functions and erf with the closed-form cdfs, the distribution relations, the multivariate Gaussian (affine maps, quadratic-form mgf, conditional law), multinomial and Dirichlet. Layer 6 already has symmetric-matrix Lebesgue measure, Cholesky with its Jacobian, the multivariate Gamma integral and the Gaussian-Gram Wishart law with its trace mgf. What remains is the real-degree density Wishart family, the spectral characteristic-function formulas, Bartlett decomposition and inverse-Wishart, which is part of one layer on existing infrastructure.
